title: A 3D human co-culture to model neuron-astrocyte interactions in tauopathies
author: Batenburg, Sestito, et al.
materials: A previously generated hiPSC line stably expressing a doxycyclin-inducible rtTA/Ngn2 [14] was maintained feeder-free on Vitronectin (Stem Cell Technologies) coated plates in TeSR-E8 medium (Stem Cell Technologies; 1X TeSR-E8 supplement (Stem Cell Technologies), 50 U/mL Pen/strep (Gibco)) supplemented with G418 (50 µg/mL; Sigma) and puromycin (0.5 µg/mL; Sigma) at 37 °C/5% CO2 under hypoxic conditions. Colonies were fed daily and double-volume feeding allowed for weekend-free culturing. Once or twice a week, colonies were passaged by non-enzymatic dissociation with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (Stem Cell Technologies) and replated in the presence of Rho-associated, coiled-coil containing protein kinase (ROCK) inhibitor (RI; 10 µM; Selleckchem) for 24 h to promote cell survival. To prevent genomic instability and senescence by prolonged passaging of hiPSCs, cryopreserved cells were thawed 2 weeks prior to use once cells reached passage number 25.

Primary human fetal astrocytes (ScienCell #1800) were cultured in Astrocyte Medium (ScienCell; 1X Growth Supplement, 1X FBS, 100 U/mL Pen/strep (all ScienCell)) on Geltrex (1:100 in DMEM/F12 (both Gibco) coated plates and half of the medium was refreshed twice a week. Astrocytes were passaged once a week by enzymatic dissociation with Accutase (Sigma). Cultures were kept at 37 °C/5% CO2 at physiological oxygen conditions and used until passage number 7. To eliminate variability in astrocyte physiology due to genetic background of the donor, all experiments in this study were conducted with cryopreserved cells that were expanded from one vial.

After one day (i.e. day -1), medium was changed to DMEM/F12 (Gibco; 1X N2 supplement, 1X NEAA, 100 U/mL Pen/strep (all Gibco)) with NT3 (10 ng/mL), BDNF (10 ng/mL) and doxycycline (2 µg/mL). At the day of co-culture (i.e. day 0), Ngn2 neural progenitors and primary human astrocytes were treated with Accutase for detachment. Prior to detachment, Accutase was aspirated and cells were dissociated separately in Neurobasal Medium (Gibco; 1X B27 + VitA, 1X Glutamax, 100 U/mL Pen/strep (all Gibco)) with NT3 (10 ng/mL), BDNF (10 ng/mL), RI (10 µM) and doxycyclin (2 µg/mL). After centrifugation the supernatant was removed and the co-culture cell suspension (30.000 neural precursors with 5.000 human astrocytes in 25 µL per well) was mixed with undiluted Geltrex (50% v/v final concentration) and kept on ice to prevent polymerization. Culture media was removed and cells were washed with PBS and fixed with paraformaldehyde (PFA), consisting of 30 min incubation at room temperature (RT) in 4% PFA (Electron Microscopy Sciences) in PBS (pH 7.4). Fixed cultures were washed once with PBS for 30 min and immediately processed for immunostaining or stored at 4 °C. For immunostaining, cells were blocked and permeabilized for 3 h in blocking solution (5% normal goat serum (Thermo Fisher) + 0.1% bovine serum albumin and 0.3% Triton X-100 (both Sigma) in PBS (pH 7.4)), and subsequently incubated with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution for 1 h at RT followed by overnight at 4 °C. After washing three times in PBS, cells were incubated overnight at 4 °C with Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies (488, 546 or 568 and 647) (Invitrogen) diluted 1:1000 in blocking solution. HS169 (1:500, a kind gift of Peter Nilsson) was used during secondary antibody incubation to label stacked beta-sheets [30]. Cells were washed three times in PBS for 15 min at RT, and cell nuclei were stained with 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) (2.5 µg/mL, Sigma) in PBS of the second wash. Confocal images were acquired with a Nikon Eclipse Ti confocal microscope equipped with a 10 × air and 40 × oil immersion objective and controlled by NisElements 4.30 software (Nikon). Z-stacks with a step size between 1 µm (for stacks < 15 µm) and 5 µm (for stacks > 15 µm) were obtained and each parameter, including laser power and detector gain, was kept constant within each experiment for valid comparison. The following primary antibodies were used: CD44 (1:100, DSHB, H4C4), Cy3-conjugated NeuroChrom (1:500, Merck, ABN2300C3), GFAP (1:1000, DAKO, Z0334), MAP2 (1:2500, Millipore, AB5543), MC1 (1:500, kind gift of Peter Davies), NF200 (1:200, Sigma, N4142), SMI312 (1:1000, Eurogentec, 312P-050), PSD95 (1:200, Abcam, AB2723), Synaptophysin 1 (1:500, Synaptic Systems, 101,004) and Tuj1 (1:1000, R&D systems, MAB1195). Maximum intensity projected Z-stacks are shown. ImageJ software (National Institute of Health) was used to adapt images for publication. Immunofluorescence data are supported by at least 3 independent experiments.

steps.title: Maintain inducible hiPSC line
steps.instruction: Culture the doxycyclin‑inducible rtTA/Ngn2 hiPSC line feeder‑free on vitronectin‑coated plates in TeSR‑E8 medium (1× supplement) with 50 U/mL penicillin/streptomycin, 50 µg/mL G418, 0.5 µg/mL puromycin at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ under hypoxic conditions; feed daily, use double‑volume feeding on weekends; passage 1–2 times /week with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent and re‑plate in the presence of 10 µM ROCK inhibitor for 24 h; thaw cryopreserved cells 2 weeks before use and keep passage number ≤ 25.

steps.title: Culture primary human astrocytes
steps.instruction: Thaw and expand ScienCell human fetal astrocytes (cat #1800) in Astrocyte Medium (1× growth supplement, 1× FBS, 100 U/mL pen/strep) on plates coated with Geltrex (1:100 in DMEM/F12); refresh half the medium twice weekly; passage weekly with Accutase; keep at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, physiological O₂; use cells up to passage 7 and only from a single cryovial to avoid donor variability.

steps.title: Induce neural progenitors (day ‑2)
steps.instruction: Two days before co‑culture, dissociate hiPSCs with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent, plate 80 000 cells per well in 6‑well plates pre‑coated with Geltrex (1:100 in DMEM/F12) in TeSR‑E8 medium supplemented with 10 ng/mL NT3, 10 ng/mL BDNF, 10 µM ROCK inhibitor, and 2 µg/mL doxycycline to induce Ngn2 expression.

steps.title: Neural progenitor maintenance (day ‑1)
steps.instruction: After 24 h, replace medium with DMEM/F12 containing 1× N2 supplement, 1× non‑essential amino acids, 100 U/mL pen/strep, 10 ng/mL NT3, 10 ng/mL BDNF, and 2 µg/mL doxycycline.

steps.title: Optional lentiviral transduction of progenitors
steps.instruction: One day before co‑culture (day ‑1), change medium to DMEM/F12 with 4 µL/mL lentiviral supernatant (CMV‑driven 2N4R FTDtau1 (P301L) or FTDtau1+2 (P301L+S320F) tagged with EGFP or mCherry). After 24 h (day 0) wash cells for 30 min with pre‑warmed Neurobasal medium containing 10 ng/mL NT3, 10 ng/mL BDNF, 10 µM ROCK inhibitor, and 2 µg/mL doxycycline to remove residual virus and prevent astrocyte transduction.

steps.title: Detach cells and prepare co‑culture suspension (day 0)
steps.instruction: Treat Ngn2 neural progenitors and primary astrocytes separately with Accutase, aspirate Accutase, and resuspend each cell type in Neurobasal medium (1× B27 + VitA, 1× Glutamax, 100 U/mL pen/strep) containing 10 ng/mL NT3, 10 ng/mL BDNF, 10 µM ROCK inhibitor, and 2 µg/mL doxycycline. Centrifuge, discard supernatant, and combine 30 000 neural progenitors with 5 000 astrocytes in 25 µL total volume per well.

steps.title: Embed cells in Geltrex and plate
steps.instruction: Mix the 25 µL cell suspension with an equal volume of undiluted Geltrex on ice to obtain a final Geltrex concentration of 50 % (v/v); keep on ice to prevent premature polymerization. Plate 50 µL of the mixture into each well of a black, high‑clarity foil‑bottom 96‑well plate (Greiner #655090), using only the inner 32 wells; fill outer wells with sterile PBS to minimize evaporation. Allow Geltrex to polymerize at 37 °C, forming a thin cylinder (≈100–200 µm thick).

steps.title: Culture and media refresh
steps.instruction: Incubate co‑cultures at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, physiological O₂. Use neuronal maturation medium (Neurobasal + B27 + VitA, 1× Glutamax, 100 U/mL pen/strep) supplemented with 10 ng/mL NT3 and 10 ng/mL BDNF. Refresh half of the medium after weeks 1 and 2, and two‑thirds after week 3, continuing weekly until week 4. Maintain cultures for at least 4 weeks (stable up to 8 weeks).

steps.title: Immunofluorescence staining
steps.instruction: Remove culture medium, wash wells with PBS, and fix cells with 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS (pH 7.4) for 30 min at room temperature. Wash once with PBS for 30 min, then block/permeabilize for 3 h in 5 % normal goat serum + 0.1 % BSA + 0.3 % Triton X‑100 in PBS. Incubate with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution for 1 h at RT followed by overnight at 4 °C (see antibody list for dilutions). Wash three times with PBS, then incubate overnight at 4 °C with Alexa Fluor‑conjugated secondary antibodies (1:1000) and HS169 (1:500) to label β‑sheet‑rich structures. Wash three times (15 min each) at RT, stain nuclei with 2.5 µg/mL DAPI during the second wash, and image with a Nikon Eclipse Ti confocal microscope (10× air or 40× oil) using identical laser and detector settings across samples. Perform maximum‑intensity projection of Z‑stacks (step size 1 µm).

substeps.instruction: Primary antibodies and dilutions: CD44 (1:100), NeuroChrom (1:500), GFAP (1:1000), MAP2 (1:2500), MC1 (1:500), NF200 (1:200), SMI312 (1:1000), PSD95 (1:200), Synaptophysin 1 (1:500), Tuj1 (1:1000).

steps.title: Calcium imaging
steps.instruction: Incubate 4‑week cultures with 1 µM Fluo‑5F‑AM in complete medium for 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Transfer plates to a heated stage (37 °C) on the Nikon Eclipse Ti confocal microscope in resonant mode (10× air objective). Acquire images at 512 × 256 px, 2× scanner zoom, 30 Hz for 10 min. Export raw fluorescence per cell, normalize each trace (0 = lowest, 1 = highest), and optionally perform post‑imaging immunostaining for β‑3‑tubulin (neurons) and GFAP (astrocytes) to assign cellular origin.

steps.title: Electron microscopy preparation
steps.instruction: Remove medium, wash once with PBS, then fix with 2.5 % glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer (pH 7.4) overnight at 4 °C. Wash three times with cacodylate buffer, post‑fix with 1 % OsO₄ and 1 % Ru(CN)₆ for 90 min at room temperature. Dehydrate through graded ethanol (30 %–100 %). Embed in EPON resin and polymerize 48 h at 65 °C. Break the 96‑well plate, locate dense cell regions by light microscopy, and cut 80 nm ultrathin sections with an Ultracut UCT microtome. Collect sections on formvar‑coated copper grids, stain with 0.5 % uranyl acetate for 25 min and lead citrate for 3 min at RT using an automated stainer. Image on a JEOL 1010 TEM at 60 kV, capturing at 40 k or 80 k magnification.

steps.title: Introduce seed‑independent tau pathology (optional)
steps.instruction: Transduce neural progenitors with EGFP‑tagged FTDtau1+2 (P301L + S320F) or mCherry‑tagged FTDtau1 (P301L) as described in the lentiviral step. After 4 weeks of co‑culture, assess tau aggregation by immunostaining for MC1 (1:500) and the thiophene dye HS169 (1:500); MC1‑positive, HS169‑positive inclusions indicate β‑sheet‑rich tau aggregates present only in FTDtau1+2‑expressing neurons.
